text:
Alex: 🚨 p99 tail spike observed on prod-runtime-1, started ~20:43 UTC. Grafana: https://graf.redwood/g/prod/runtime-tail?orgId=1
Priya: on it, link to trace?
Alex: trace attached in alert: trace_id=trc_0x8f33. p95 up 3x, p99 up 6x for long-context (seq>2048). Throughput steady.
Jordan: initial gut: admission/backpressure or fallback to slow kernel. I saw kernel-selector log noise earlier.
Ravi: checking kvcache evictions now, running `curl` against metrics endpoint on the node group: `curl -s http://10.2.4.11:9100/metrics | grep kvcache_evictions`
Ravi: small snippet from node logs:
```
2026-02-12T20:42:59Z kernel-selector: picked=fast_kernel_v2 seq=128 latency_est=8ms
2026-02-12T20:43:01Z kernel-selector: picked=emulate_kernel seq=4096 fallback=true reason=kv_miss
2026-02-12T20:43:02Z admission: microbatch_wait=24ms queue_len=42
2026-02-12T20:43:02Z kvcache: evict_count=128 recent_hit_ratio=0.22
```
Elena: `emulate_kernel` shows up when we run out of fused kernels for long sequences — that explains p99. But why the sudden kv miss?
Priya: did a quick heap/IO check, disk io ~ normal, GPU util unchanged. Could be noisy neighbor on kvcache shard. Which shard for node-11?
Alex: node-11 handles shards 7 and 8. Marta and I rolled a kernel config change to canary last week that widened allowed sequence thresholds. Could be related.
Marta: I rolled a config bump at 19:30 UTC: `kernel.selector.max_seq_for_fast=2048 -> 4096` to reduce fallbacks for medium-long requests. Might have unintended consequence on kernel binary selection.
Jordan: interesting. If selection window increased, the kernel selector may attempt fast_kernel_v2 for seqs up to 4096 but fallback happens to emulate_kernel due to missing fused kernels on some GPUs, causing latency cliff. Also admission queue increases because the emulation path is slower per-token.
Ravi: started a profile capture for the affected node group (30s perf record + nvprof). Saving to s3://redwood-profiles/1919001123-node11.tar.gz
SRE Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2142, slack-thread=1919001123, paging oncall.
Priya: temporary mitigation: revert config or lower max_seq_for_fast back to 2048? That will force the selector to use stable kernel candidates.
Alex: can we hotpatch admission to lower max_inflight_per_worker by 20% to reduce queue pressure?
Jordan: yes, we can push a soft-limit change: `admission.max_inflight=120 -> 95` on target pool. I'll do it and watch latency.
Elena: Also need to check KV shard replication lag — if a shard was temporarily slow, that explains kv miss ratio spike. Running `kubectl exec -c runtime -- /bin/sh -c "redis-cli info"` against shard7.
Marta: rolling back the canary now. Patch queued, will apply in 30s.
Ravi: profile upload complete, attaching top-heavy stack sample showing `kv_get` blocking and fallback kernel `run_emulate` hot:
```
samples:
  run_emulate: 47.2%
  kv_get (network): 22.7%
  admission::wait_loop: 12.1%
```
Priya: rollback confirmed applied on all canary nodes. Also lowered admission limit as Jordan suggested.
Alex: after rollback, p99 dropped back to normal within 40s. trace shows fewer `emulate_kernel` events. Current graphs: p99 ~ baseline.
Jordan: root cause hypothesis: canary widened acceptable seq range, causing selector to attempt fast kernels on nodes without the fused kernel build -> frequent fallbacks to slow emulate path + increased kvcache pressure (evictions) -> admission queueing -> tail spike.
Marta: follow-ups: (1) add a preflight check in canary rollout to verify kernel binaries exist on all target images for any seq windows changed, (2) add metric `kernel.selector.fallback_reason` to monitor fallback patterns, (3) tighten kvcache observability (per-shard hit ratios), (4) add automated rollback if fallback_rate > 1% for 5m.
Elena: creating a short postmortem draft and action items. I'll include the timeline and the commands we ran.
Alex: thanks everyone. Assigning owners: Marta -> rollout preflight checks + automated rollback, Jordan -> admission autoscaling/playbook, Ravi -> profile artifact retention and tooling, Priya -> dashboards/alerts for kernel fallback rate.
Priya: small note: add a test in CI that simulates missing fused kernel by toggling feature flag to ensure the selector doesn't flip to a slower path at scale.
Marta: will follow up with a PR linking to this thread.
Alex: closing the immediate incident — monitoring for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
